thread.title: Tech Is Tumbling…and It’s About a Lot More Than Just Twitter and Facebook

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Tech Is Tumbling…and It’s About a Lot More Than Just Twitter and Facebook
text:
By Ben Levisohn Updated Sept. 6, 2018 1:34 p.m. ET Stocks are heading lower today, and once again tech stocks including Twitter (TWTR) and Facebook (FB) are to blame.
Where we were: Tech has been the best-performing sector this year, as investors piled into stocks like Apple (AAPL), Amazon.com (AMZN), and Facebook (FB).
Where we're headed: Tech sold off yesterday, and is under pressure again today. While it's easy to point at concerns about regulation, tech's underperformance actually began around earnings season. Many of the stocks are popular with hedge fund managers, who appear to be rightsizing their portfolios.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average has declined 42.65 points, or 0.2%, to 25,932.34, while the S&P 500 has fallen 0.5% to 2874.24 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has dropped 0.9% to 7923.01. The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) has slumped 1% to $73.65, as stocks like Twitter (TWTR), Facebook (FB), and Alphabet (GOOGL), which were in the spotlight on Capitol Hill yesterday , get hit.
But they're not the only ones. Micron Technology (MU), down 8.7% at $45.23, and KLA-Tencor (KLAC), off 9.1% at $108.03, are today's worst performers after Micron's CFO said NAND prices was falling . As we mentioned yesterday, the hearings might have been one catalyst, but this selloff in tech isn't just about fears of regulation .
All this comes at a particularly bad time for these tech stocks. In a note released last night, Lori Calvasina , head of U.S. equity strategy at RBC Capital Markets, noted that many have "crowding and/or valuation problems." Nine of the 10 most popular stocks with growth-fund managers come from tech and internet groups, while 13 of the 20 most popular stocks with hedge funds came from those groups as well, Calvasina observes.
The wave of selling didn't come out of nowhere. The most popular stocks with hedge funds have been lagging the S&P 500 since late June, while the most popular with growth managers have been lagging since late July.
" A tough 2Q earnings season , in which many of these names beat on EPS but disappointed on revenues, guidance or some other metric, was responsible for some of that underperformance," Calvasina writes. "We suspect hedge fund derisking has also been at play, and think profit taking in these names, which have generally seen strong outperformance in 2018, remains a risk as we start to approach year end."
And regulation has little, if anything, to do with it.
Make the Connection
• While the selloff in emerging markets and U.S. tech stocks might not seem to have a lot in common, the Nasdaq's tumble could be the first sign that the stress overseas is starting to have an impact at home.
• Another victim of the tech wreck: Amazon's $1 trillion market capitalization. Since touching $2,050.50 on Monday, the stock has dropped 5.1% to $1,945.52 at 1:29 p.m. today.
